How to reset the board after the other congregation

beginner · about 7 min · updated 2026-05-11

We share our sound board with another congregation. They have a different service style, different mics, and a different mix. Every Sunday we have to bring the board back to OUR known-good state before our service starts.

This article walks through the procedure for both boards (digital and analog). It assumes you’ve already looked at the Reset the board page and want to understand WHY we do it this way.

Step 1: Arrive early

Plan to be at the board at least 30 minutes before the service. Resetting takes 5–10 minutes, plus you still need to do a sound check.

Step 2: Take a phone photo BEFORE you change anything

Before you touch the board, photograph its current state. This serves two purposes:

  1. If something breaks during YOUR setup, you can see what changed.
  2. If the other congregation’s team complains that you broke something, you have a record of what they left.

Step 3 (Digital board): Load the saved scene

On the digital board, press the SCENES button and load Scene 1: Sunday Morning. The board will move every fader, every gain knob, every EQ setting back to the saved state in one step.

After loading, compare the board against the photo on the Reset page. If anything looks different, it means either the scene was saved wrong, or the other team has been editing the scene rather than creating their own. In that case, follow the analog procedure below for the wrong channels.

Step 3 (Analog board): Compare channel by channel

The analog board has no memory. You have to compare every channel against the photo and per-channel notes. Work left to right:

  1. Check the channel name strip and verify it matches the photo.
  2. Compare the gain (TRIM) knob position. Should be at the marked spot.
  3. Compare the EQ knobs — usually all at 12 o’clock (flat) unless noted.
  4. Compare the AUX sends for the monitor mix.
  5. Compare the fader position.
  6. Check MUTE status — if a red LED is on but the photo shows it off, unmute. And vice versa.
  7. Move to the next channel.

This takes 5–10 minutes for a full board. Don’t rush.

Step 4: Sound check ONE input

Before the band arrives, plug in one wired mic (a Shure SM58 is perfect for this) and check that you hear it cleanly through the main mix AND through the monitor mix. If you do, the signal chain is intact.

If you don’t, don’t start tweaking — start with the troubleshooting checklist for no sound.

Step 5: Save again (digital only) — but ONLY when correct

If you had to fix the digital scene, save it back as the same scene number. If you’re not 100% sure the corrections are right, don’t save over the known-good scene — talk to the deacon first.

For the analog board, take a new photo of the corrected state and upload it through the CMS so the next volunteer has the latest reference.

When to escalate

If the board’s state is dramatically different from the photo — for example, channels are routed to outputs you don’t recognize, or sub-groups have been reassigned — that’s beyond a normal reset. Stop, ask an experienced person, and consider it a recurring issue worth logging.

Suggestions on this site are guidance, not professional advice. If you are unsure, stop and ask an experienced sound engineer.
